Date: 2026-06-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO, Peregrine), Maya Chen (Eng Mgr), Ethan Ross (SRE)
Recording: yes
Notes: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, and token/sec benchmarking. AE + SE present from Redwood.
summary: Peregrine Payments is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted + dedicated deployment. Primary success criteria are 100-150ms p95 for short chat flows (<=256 tokens) and sub-400ms p95 for longer streaming flows up to 1k tokens; concurrency expected 150-300 concurrent user sessions with bursts to 800. They asked about streaming latency, KV/prefix caching, quantization impact, and fallbacks between hosted/dedicated/private. Agreed next steps: send benchmark template, provision hosted trial for token/sec tests, share SOC2/security docs, and schedule pricing follow-up for dedicated capacity.
topics: p95 targets and how Redwood measures p95
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Sofia from Redwood, I'm here with Liam our systems engineer. Quick intros?
[00:08] Raj: Raj Patel, CTO at Peregrine. We're looking at options for putting LLM features in payments fraud detection and customer support.
[00:14] Maya: Maya, engineering manager, I'm driving infra decisions.
[00:18] Ethan: Ethan, SRE. I'll poke at the numbers.
[00:22] Liam: Great, thanks. Goal for today is to understand your p95 targets, concurrency, streaming needs, and which deployment model you're leaning toward.
[00:33] Raj: High level, we have two main workloads: a short chat assistant (mostly <=256 tokens) and a longer analysis job that can stream up to 1k tokens. For chat we need p95 around 100-150ms; for longer streaming it's okay to be up to 400ms p95 but we care about steady token/sec rates.
[00:52] Sofia: Okay that's really helpful. Are those p95 numbers end-to-end from client to response or just token generation time?
[00:58] Raj: End-to-end from our API gateway to final token. Our SLAs with customers are tight.
[01:03] Liam: Understood. For hosted Redwood we'd measure p95 end-to-end on our side but you can also run the benchmark from your infra to include network. We typically report both median and p95 and we surface per-route breakdowns in Console.
[01:18] Maya: Concurrency — current plan is 150 steady concurrent users during business hours, with seasonal bursts up to 800 for promos. Each user is an interactive session, so open streaming connections matter.
[01:29] Ethan: And for throughput, we're targeting sustained 1k tokens/sec for the analysis pipeline during batch windows, and burst token/sec of 3-4k for short spikes.
[01:38] Liam: Right, so two different constraints: latency-sensitive short flows and throughput-sensitive streaming flows. For the chat flow, to hit 100-150ms p95 for <=256 tokens we recommend dedicated capacity or a high-tier hosted plan with pinned capacity. If you go hosted shared, you can still get close but we'd recommend autoscale buffers and prefix caching.
[01:57] Raj: How much does quantization affect latency? We're considering 4-bit quantized models to save cost.
[02:03] Liam: Good question — quantization often reduces memory and can lower throughput latency marginally on some kernels, but it can also increase compute overhead if the hardware path isn't optimal. Our runtime selects kernels; for many open models 4-bit can give 10-20% cost improvement and similar or slightly improved latency for longer tokens, but for ultra-low p95 targets on short sequences sometimes full fp16 on right hardware is better. We'll profile on your target model.
[02:28] Maya: What about streaming? We need first-token latency to be low and steady per token generation thereafter.
[02:34] Liam: Streaming adds small per-token overhead. If you do continuous streaming with small tokens, batching can hurt first-token latency. We support split routing — we'll keep low-latency requests on low-batch lanes and route high-throughput streaming to batching-optimized lanes. You can also enable prefix/KV caching to avoid recomputing the context.
[02:52] Raj: Can you handle 800 concurrent streaming connections?
[02:56] Liam: Yes with Dedicated we can provision enough workers and autoscale. For hosted, we recommend reserved capacity or a hybrid approach — keep baseline on dedicated and overflow to hosted. We also have fallback policies to use lower-cost variants when capacity constrained.
[03:10] Sofia: Quick clarify on measurements — when you say p95 150ms, that's including network, right?
[03:15] Liam: We report both. For this call we'll send a benchmark harness you can run from your infra that hits our hosted endpoints to capture real end-to-end p95. We'll also run internal benchmarks on similar nodes to show model-only delta.
[03:29] Ethan: About KV cache, we've got a lot of repeated prefixes for fraud checks; can Redwood cache those?
[03:35] Liam: Yes, prefix/KV caching is supported. We can keep session-level caches for active users to cut down token compute on replays. That helps both latency and cost. Note that cache hit rate drives savings, so we'd want a sample of your session distribution.
[03:49] Raj: Security — SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO, VPC peering. We might need on-prem eventually.
[03:57] Sofia: We have SOC2 and ISO artifacts; we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments and provide audit logs and RBAC in the Console. For VPC/on-prem we'd use Redwood Private with a private control plane. We'll attach security docs after this call.
[04:12] Maya: For benchmarks, what payloads do you need?
[04:15] Liam: Ideally sample prompts across both workloads: typical chat prompt (<=256), typical streaming prompt (1k tokens), and a distribution file showing token lengths and concurrency patterns. We'll include a template.
[04:27] Raj: Okay. Cost — can you ballpark cost differences between hosted vs dedicated for our expected load?
[04:33] Sofia: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet after we get the benchmark numbers. Roughly, Dedicated with reserved GPUs gives predictable unit cost and lower p95 variance; hosted is cheaper up-front but you pay a premium on peak. We'll include an amortized token/sec cost model in the spreadsheet.
[04:50] Ethan: For the analysis pipeline, we need sustained 1k token/sec — can hosted handle sustained throughput or do we need dedicated?
[04:57] Liam: Hosted can for many cases, but for sustained high throughput with predictable latency you often choose Dedicated. We recommend a POC on hosted first to validate model and correctness, then move to Dedicated for production throughput guarantees.
[05:10] Raj: Can we do an initial run with, say, 500 concurrent sessions, streaming 2-3 tokens per second per session to simulate bursts?
[05:16] Liam: Yep — we'll provision a test harness. We'll also instrument per-token latency and per-route breakdown so you can see where time is spent (network, queuing, generation).
[05:27] Maya: How do you handle backpressure during bursts?
[05:30] Liam: Autoscaling + smart routing. We also have queueing policies and graceful degradation where requests can be routed to lower-latency smaller models or fall back to cached responses depending on policy.
[05:41] Raj: Any known gotchas around GPU kernel selection and short sequence p95?
[05:45] Liam: For very short sequences the kernel overhead and dispatch latency matter more. Our runtime has specialized kernels for short sequences and fast attention paths, but some open model variants and quantization combos can increase dispatch overhead. We'll profile and pick the best kernel/quant combo.
[05:58] [crosstalk]
[06:02] Sofia: We'll include recommended quantization profiles per model in the benchmark output.
[06:06] Ethan: What's the typical timeline for a dedicated capacity onboarding if we decide to commit?
[06:11] Sofia: Usually 4-8 weeks depending on capacity size and network setup; Private on-prem can be longer. We'll give a more precise timeline in the pricing follow-up.
[06:20] Raj: For the baseline POC can you share an SLA we can expect?
[06:24] Sofia: For hosted trial there's no SLA; for Dedicated we include SLA options in the contract. We'll attach a sample SLA doc.
[06:31] Maya: How do you measure p95? Rolling window? Over what period?
[06:36] Liam: We compute percentiles over a sliding window and show both rolling and daily aggregates in Console. We'll also provide raw traces for the benchmark runs.
[06:45] Raj: Ok, anything else — streaming token/sec benchmarking specifics?
[06:50] Liam: We'll run three tests: 1) short sequence latency test (50-256 tokens) to capture first-token and final-token p95; 2) sustained streaming token/sec test to measure steady-state tokens/sec while tracking per-token latency; 3) burst test simulating 800 concurrent short sessions. We'll report p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU util, batch sizes, and kernel selection.
[07:12] Sofia: We'll include a spreadsheet with columns for your reported p95 targets, our measured p95, delta, cost estimate, and recommended deployment.
[07:21] Raj: Sounds good. Who's doing what after this call?
[07:24] Sofia: I'll send the benchmark template, pricing starter, and SOC2 docs. Liam will provision the hosted trial and run baseline tests, Raj will share payloads and concurrency profile.
[07:33] Maya: One more question — do you support token-level tracing for debugging outliers?
[07:38] Liam: Yes, Console has traces with per-token timing. We can also provide sampling of full traces for your team.
[07:44] Ethan: For the stream architecture, is there support for HTTP/2 or websockets? We prefer websockets for many of our clients.
[07:50] Liam: We support HTTP streaming and websockets; we'll include endpoints in the trial.
[07:55] Raj: Any requirements from our networking side for VPC peering or do you provide a private link?
[07:59] Sofia: For Redwood Private we support VPC peering and private link setups; we'll include network checklist.
[08:06] [long pause while notes are exchanged]
[08:18] Sofia: Quick recap: benchmark template, hosted trial, SOC2 docs, pricing follow-up. Next call to review benchmark results and dedicated pricing.
[08:28] Raj: Good. Thanks everyone.
[08:31] Maya: Thanks.
[08:33] Ethan: Thanks.
[08:35] Liam: Thanks, we'll send materials by end of day Friday.
[08:39] Sofia: Bye.
[08:40] [call ends]
